column3: BSB supplies “Jesus” and renders the present-tense “comes” and “follow” as past, recasting the following as accompaniment.
“Ideas” interprets “these things.” The Greek describes mighty works being done through His hands rather than asking how He can perform them.

The Greek specifically names copper rather than the more general “money.”
BSB renders “two tunics” as “a second tunic.”
“That area” makes the Greek “from there” more explicit.
BSB follows the critical text without the saying about Sodom and Gomorrah found in the Textus Receptus (Σοδόμοις). The Greek speaks of a place that does not receive them, rather than “anyone.”
“The people” makes the unspecified subject of repentance explicit.
BSB places healing before anointing; the Greek has driving out demons, anointing the sick, then healing them.
“Jesus” makes the possessive referent explicit. The Greek says John “has been raised,” rather than the active “has risen.”
“Of old” is not explicitly present in the Greek.
BSB’s “from the dead” matches the Textus Receptus (νεκρῶν); the critical text has only “was raised.”
BSB recasts Herod’s sending, seizing and binding John as an order for his arrest and imprisonment.
